items.stem: A substance X is used as a building material and is insoluble in water. When it reacts with dil. HCl, it produces a gas which turns lime water milky. (i) Write the chemical name and formula of 'X'. (ii) Write chemical equations for the chemical reactions involved in the above statements.
items.answer: (i) Substance X is calcium carbonate. Chemical formula: CaCO₃. (ii) Calcium carbonate reacts with dilute hydrochloric acid to give calcium chloride, water and carbon dioxide: CaCO₃(s) + 2HCl(aq) → CaCl₂(aq) + H₂O(l) + CO₂(g). The carbon dioxide evolved reacts with lime water, Ca(OH)₂, to form calcium carbonate and water: Ca(OH)₂(aq) + CO₂(g) → CaCO₃(s) + H₂O(l). The insoluble calcium carbonate produced is responsible for the milky white colour.
items.ocr: MinerU dropped both reaction arrows; → restored from the worked solution. LaTeX artefacts ^CaCl2h and ^CO2h rewritten as CaCl₂ and CO₂; 'Ca OHh2' read as Ca(OH)₂. Printed solution writes H₂O(aq); given as H₂O(l).

items.stem: (i) A compound 'A' with a molecular formula of C₂H₆O reacts with a base to give salt and water. Identify 'A', state its nature and the name of the functional group it possesses. Write chemical equation for the reaction involved. (ii) When the above stated compound 'A' reacts with another compound 'B' having molecular formula C₂H₆O in the presence of an acid, a sweet smelling compound 'C' is formed. (1) Identify 'B' and 'C'. (2) State the role of acid in this reaction. (3) Write chemical equation for the reaction involved.
items.answer: (i) Compound A is acetic acid (ethanoic acid), CH₃COOH. Its nature is acidic and the functional group it possesses is the carboxyl group, –COOH. CH₃COOH(aq) + NaOH(aq) → CH₃COONa(aq) + H₂O(l). (ii) (1) B is ethanol, C₂H₅OH, and C is ethyl acetate / ethyl ethanoate, CH₃COOC₂H₅. (2) The acid is a catalyst; it speeds up the process so that esterification proceeds quickly and goes to completion. (3) C₂H₅OH + CH₃COOH --conc. H₂SO₄--> CH₃COOC₂H₅ + H₂O.
items.ocr: The printed stem gives A the formula C₂H₆O, but the worked solution identifies A as acetic acid (C₂H₄O₂); the solution wins for the answer while the stem is kept as printed. The question is split by MinerU's reading order (it ends mid-sentence on the page-29 block and continues at the head of the page-28 block); the two halves were rejoined. Reaction arrows restored.

items.stem: (i) Name the compound formed when ethanol is heated at 443 K in the presence of conc. H₂SO₄ and draw its electron dot structure. State the role of conc. H₂SO₄ in this reaction. (ii) What is hydrogenation? Explain it with the help of a chemical equation. State the role of this reaction in industry.
items.answer: (i) Ethyl alcohol (ethanol) is converted into ethene: CH₃CH₂OH --conc. H₂SO₄, 443 K--> CH₂=CH₂ + H₂O. In the electron dot structure of ethene the two carbon atoms share two electron pairs with each other (a double bond) and each carbon shares one electron pair with each of two hydrogen atoms. Role of conc. H₂SO₄: it acts as a dehydrating agent and removes a molecule of water from ethanol. (ii) Hydrogenation is the process in which unsaturated compounds react with hydrogen in the presence of a catalyst such as nickel to form saturated compounds: R₂C=CR₂ + H₂ --Ni/Pt/Pd--> R₂CH–CHR₂. Role in industry: it is used for the hydrogenation of vegetable oils, whose long unsaturated carbon chains are converted into vegetable ghee, i.e. saturated fats.
items.ocr: Reaction arrows restored from the solution. The stem prints the condition as 443 K while the solution's equation prints 160–170 °C; both describe the same dehydration. The electron dot structure is printed as a worked-solution figure, so no image is attached.

items.stem: 'Carbon forms strong bonds with most other elements making the compounds exceptionally stable.' Give reason to justify this statement.
items.answer: Carbon has 4 electrons in its outermost shell and requires 4 more electrons to attain a noble gas electronic configuration. It cannot form a positive ion, because a huge amount of energy is required to remove 4 valence electrons and the ion so formed would have 6 protons and only 2 electrons, making it highly unstable. It cannot form a negative ion either, because a nucleus with only 6 protons cannot hold 10 electrons against the inter-electronic repulsion. So carbon achieves a noble gas configuration only by sharing its 4 valence electrons with other atoms, forming strong covalent bonds. The two main reasons carbon forms a large number of such stable compounds are: (a) Catenation – the ability of carbon to form bonds with other carbon atoms, giving long chains, branched chains and rings; (b) Tetravalency – carbon has 4 valence electrons, so it can form covalent bonds with 4 other atoms.
items.ocr: Printed line 'its nucleus with 6 protons cannot 10 electrons' is missing a verb; read as 'cannot hold 10 electrons'.

items.stem: Which compounds are called (i) alkanes, (ii) alkenes and (iii) alkynes? C₄H₁₀ belongs to which of these? Draw two structural isomers of this compound.
items.answer: (i) The hydrocarbons in which carbon atoms are connected by only single covalent bonds are called alkanes. (ii) The hydrocarbons in which carbon atoms are connected by a double bond are called alkenes. (iii) The hydrocarbons in which carbon atoms are connected by a triple bond are called alkynes. C₄H₁₀ belongs to the alkanes. Its two structural isomers are: (a) n-butane, CH₃–CH₂–CH₂–CH₃; (b) iso-butane (2-methylpropane), CH₃–CH(CH₃)–CH₃, i.e. a three-carbon chain carrying a CH₃ branch on the middle carbon.
items.ocr: The answer is split by MinerU's page ordering: 'C₄H₁₀ belongs to alkane. Structural Isomers of C₄H₁₀ ...' appears after the page-29/30 block and was rejoined here. Isomer (b) prints as a stacked LaTeX drawing; rewritten in linear form. Page furniture 'Downloaded from www.pdf.tube' stripped.

items.stem: Write the chemical formula and name of the compound which is the active ingredient of all alcoholic drinks. List its two uses. Write chemical equation and name of the product formed when this compound reacts with (i) sodium metal (ii) hot concentrated sulphuric acid.
items.answer: The active ingredient of alcoholic drinks is ethanol; its formula is C₂H₅OH. Two uses of ethanol: (1) it is used as a solvent in various industries; (2) it is used as an antiseptic solution. (i) Reaction with sodium metal: 2C₂H₅OH + 2Na → 2C₂H₅ONa + H₂. The product is sodium ethoxide, and hydrogen gas is evolved. (ii) Reaction with hot conc. H₂SO₄ (at 443 K): C₂H₅OH --conc. H₂SO₄--> CH₂=CH₂ + H₂O. The product is ethene; conc. H₂SO₄ acts as a dehydrating agent.
items.ocr: Reaction arrows restored. The printed sodium equation is unbalanced (C₂H₅OH + Na → C₂H₅ONa + H₂); balanced here. The printed label 'Sodium ethanoate' under C₂H₅ONa contradicts the product itself, which is sodium ethoxide; corrected.

items.stem: What is methane? Draw its electron dot structure. Name the type of bonds formed in this compound. Why are such compounds: (i) poor conductors of electricity? and (ii) have low melting and boiling points? What happens when this compound burns in oxygen?
items.answer: Methane is a hydrocarbon formed by the combination of carbon with hydrogen. Its molecular formula is CH₄ and it is a main greenhouse gas. In its electron dot structure the carbon atom shares one electron pair with each of four hydrogen atoms, so the type of bond formed in methane is the covalent bond. (i) Covalent compounds are poor conductors of electricity because they are formed by the sharing of electrons and have no free electrons (or ions) available to conduct electricity. (ii) They have weak forces of attraction between their molecules, so little energy is required to break these forces; hence they have low melting and boiling points. When methane burns in oxygen a combustion reaction takes place: CH₄ + 2O₂ → CO₂ + 2H₂O + heat + light.
items.ocr: Printed combustion equation shows O₂ written over the arrow and is unbalanced; rewritten balanced as CH₄ + 2O₂ → CO₂ + 2H₂O. Printed 'Methane s a hydrocarbon ormed by' repaired to 'is a hydrocarbon formed by'. Electron dot figure belongs to the worked solution, so no image is attached.

items.stem: (a) Why are most carbon compounds poor conductors of electricity? (b) Write the name and structure of a saturated compound in which the carbon atoms are arranged in a ring. Give the number of single bonds present in this compound.
items.answer: (a) Electricity is conducted by moving electrons (or ions). Carbon forms covalent bonds by sharing electrons, so carbon compounds do not have free electrons or ions and are therefore poor conductors of electricity. (b) Cyclohexane, C₆H₁₂, is a saturated compound in which the carbon atoms are arranged in a ring: six carbon atoms joined in a closed hexagonal ring, each carbon also carrying two hydrogen atoms. There are 6 carbon–carbon single bonds present in the ring of this compound.
items.ocr: Printed answer label 'd Electricity is conducted...' is a damaged '(a)'. The cyclohexane structure is a worked-solution figure, so no image is attached.

items.stem: A compound 'X' on heating with excess conc. sulphuric acid at 443 K gives an unsaturated compound 'Y'. 'X' also reacts with sodium metal to evolve a colourless gas 'Z'. Identify 'X', 'Y' and 'Z'. Write the equation of the chemical reaction of formation of 'Y' and also write the role of sulphuric acid in the reaction.
items.answer: X = CH₃CH₂OH (ethanol); Y = CH₂=CH₂ (ethene); Z = hydrogen gas, H₂. Formation of Y: CH₃CH₂OH --conc. H₂SO₄, 443 K--> CH₂=CH₂ + H₂O. With sodium metal: 2CH₃CH₂OH + 2Na → 2CH₃CH₂ONa + H₂. Here concentrated sulphuric acid acts as a dehydrating agent; it removes a water molecule from ethanol.
items.ocr: The printed stem lost the letter in 'formation of ' ' '; restored to 'Y' from the solution. The identifications of X, Y and Z sit far away in the MinerU output (at the head of the page-34 block) and were rejoined. The sodium equation printed unbalanced; balanced here. Reaction arrows restored.

items.stem: You are given ball and stick models of six carbon atoms and fourteen hydrogen atoms and a sufficient number of sticks. In how many ways can one join the models of six carbon atoms and fourteen hydrogen atoms to form different molecules of C₆H₁₄?
items.answer: Five ways. C₆H₁₄ (hexane) has five structural isomers, so five types of molecules can be made with these balls and sticks. The five isomers are: n-hexane (CH₃CH₂CH₂CH₂CH₂CH₃), 2-methylpentane, 3-methylpentane, 2,2-dimethylbutane and 2,3-dimethylbutane.
items.ocr: Printed stem reads 'balls and stick model'; smoothed to 'ball and stick models'. The five isomer structures are printed only as worked-solution figures, so no image is attached and the isomers are named in words.

items.stem: Draw the structural formulae of all the possible isomers of the compound with the molecular formula C₃H₆O and also give their electron dot structures.
items.answer: There are two possible isomers of C₃H₆O: (i) propanal, C₂H₅CHO, i.e. CH₃–CH₂–CHO, in which the aldehyde (–CHO) group is at the end of the chain; and (ii) propanone, CH₃COCH₃, in which the carbonyl (>C=O) group is on the middle carbon. In their electron dot structures every C–H and C–C bond is one shared electron pair, while the carbon–oxygen bond of the carbonyl group is two shared electron pairs, the oxygen atom also carrying two lone pairs of electrons.
items.ocr: The two structures print as damaged stacked LaTeX drawings (carbon chains rendered with extra 'C's) plus a worked-solution figure; rewritten in linear form from the names given in the solution. No image attached because the figures belong to the solution.

items.stem: Two carbon compounds A and B have the molecular formulae C₃H₈ and C₃H₆ respectively. (a) Which one of the two is most likely to show addition reaction? Justify your answer. (b) Explain with the help of chemical equation, how an addition reaction is useful in vegetable ghee industry.
items.answer: (a) C₃H₆ (compound B) will show the addition reaction, as it is an unsaturated hydrocarbon containing a carbon–carbon double bond. C₃H₆ reacts with hydrogen in the presence of a catalyst to give propane by adding one molecule of hydrogen across the double bond: C₃H₆ + H₂ → C₃H₈. (b) Vegetable oils contain long unsaturated carbon chains. Vegetable oil reacts with hydrogen in the presence of nickel as a catalyst to form vegetable ghee, which is a saturated compound: R–CH=CH–R + H₂ --Ni--> R–CH₂–CH₂–R, i.e. vegetable oil (unsaturated) + H₂ --Ni--> vegetable ghee (saturated).
items.ocr: The bank also prints an 'or' variant of this question ('...how an addition reaction is useful in industries'); the main wording is kept. The vegetable-oil equation prints as badly mangled LaTeX; rewritten from the labels 'Vegetable oil (Unsaturated)', 'Ni' and 'Vegetable ghee (Saturated)'.

items.stem: (a) Give chemical tests to detect the presence of (i) Ethanol (ii) Ethanoic acid. (b) Why is ethanoic acid called glacial acetic acid?
items.answer: (a) (i) Test for ethanol – reaction with sodium: reactive metals like Na liberate hydrogen gas, which is combustible and burns with a pop sound. 2CH₃CH₂OH + 2Na → 2CH₃CH₂O⁻Na⁺ + H₂(g) (sodium ethoxide). (ii) Test for ethanoic acid – esterification: esters are formed by the reaction of an acid with an alcohol, so on warming ethanoic acid with ethanol in the presence of a few drops of conc. H₂SO₄ a sweet, fruity smelling ester is obtained. CH₃COOH + CH₃CH₂OH --conc. H₂SO₄, Δ--> CH₃COOC₂H₅ + H₂O. (b) The melting point of pure ethanoic acid is 290 K, so it often freezes during winter in cold climates and looks like ice. This gives rise to its name, glacial acetic acid.
items.ocr: The esterification equation prints with a broken arrow and scrambled labels ('Acid / Ethanoic acid / Ethane', 'CH C - OCH CH₃'); rewritten as CH₃COOC₂H₅ from the reactants shown. Reaction arrows restored.

items.stem: What are micelles? How does the formation of a micelle help to clean the clothes?
items.answer: Soap molecules consist of two parts – one part is hydrophobic (the long hydrocarbon tail, which dissolves in oil and grease) and the other part is hydrophilic (the ionic head, which dissolves in water). When soap is dissolved in water it forms groups of many molecules known as micelles. In these groups the hydrophobic tails point into the interior of the group and the ionic ends lie on the surface, facing the water. Soap in the form of a micelle is able to clean a dirty cloth because the oily dirt is collected in the centre of the micelle, held by the hydrocarbon tails, while the ionic ends keep the micelle suspended in water. When the water is agitated, the dirt sticks to the micelles and is pulled away from the cloth; rinsing then washes the dirt-laden micelles away with the water and the cloth becomes clean.
items.ocr: The printed solution is cut off by a page break at 'When water is agitated, the dirt sticks to'; the sentence was completed from the cleansing-action explanation printed elsewhere in the same chapter. The micelle diagram is a worked-solution figure, so no image is attached.

items.stem: What is an oxidizing agent? What happens when an oxidizing agent is added to propanol? Explain with the help of a chemical equation.
items.answer: (i) An oxidising agent is a substance which can give oxygen to other substances (or remove hydrogen from them). (ii) When an oxidising agent such as alkaline KMnO₄ or acidified K₂Cr₂O₇ is added to propanol, the propanol is oxidised to propanoic acid: CH₃–CH₂–CH₂–OH --alkaline KMnO₄ or acidified K₂Cr₂O₇--> CH₃–CH₂–COOH (propanoic acid). (iii) So propanol is oxidised to propanoic acid.
items.ocr: The reagent line prints as damaged LaTeX ('Alkalme NMno 0₄ / or Acidified K₂Cr₂O₇'); read as alkaline KMnO₄ or acidified K₂Cr₂O₇. The product drawn as a stacked structure with a separate 'O'; rewritten as CH₃CH₂COOH, which matches the printed label 'Propanoic acid'. Arrow restored.

items.stem: When ethanol reacts with ethanoic acid in the presence of conc. H₂SO₄, a substance with fruity smell is produced. Answer the following: (i) State the class of compounds to which the fruity smelling compounds belong. Write the chemical equation for the reaction and write the chemical name of the product formed. (ii) State the role of conc. H₂SO₄.
items.answer: (i) The fruity smelling compounds belong to the class of esters. CH₃COOH + CH₃CH₂OH --conc. H₂SO₄--> CH₃COOC₂H₅ + H₂O. The chemical name of the product formed is ethyl ethanoate. (ii) Conc. H₂SO₄ acts as a dehydrating agent; it helps in the removal of the water formed in the reaction and so drives the esterification forward.
items.ocr: The printed ester equation is garbled LaTeX ('CH₃–C(=O)–O–CH₃–CH₂O–CH₂–CH₃'); rewritten as CH₃COOC₂H₅ + H₂O, which is what the printed product name 'ethyl ethanoate' requires. Arrow restored.

items.stem: When ethanol reacts with ethanoic acid in the presence of conc. H₂SO₄, a substance with fruity smell is produced. Answer the following: (i) State the class of compounds to which the fruity smelling compounds belong. Write the chemical equation for the reaction and write the chemical name of the product formed. (ii) State the role of conc. H₂SO₄ in this reaction.
items.answer: (i) The class of compounds to which the fruity smelling compounds belong is esters. CH₃COOH + C₂H₅OH --conc. H₂SO₄--> CH₃COOC₂H₅ + H₂O; here ethanoic acid and ethanol give ethyl ethanoate (an ester). The solution also prints a second example: C₃H₇COOH + C₂H₅OH --conc. H₂SO₄--> C₃H₇COOC₂H₅ + H₂O, i.e. butanoic acid with ethanol. (ii) The role of conc. H₂SO₄ in this reaction is that of a catalyst.
items.ocr: This is a near-duplicate of printed question 233; both are kept because the bank prints them as separate numbered questions with different year tags and different printed answers (233 calls conc. H₂SO₄ a dehydrating agent, 234 calls it a catalyst). Reaction arrows restored from LaTeX that printed the condition as '_Onc.H₃SO₄'.

items.stem: (i) Chemical properties of ethanol is different from methyl ethanoate. Justify the statement with proper reason. (ii) Methyl ethanoate is used in making perfume. Justify. (iii) Ethanol is converted into ethene with excess of hot concentrated H₂SO₄. Justify with the help of chemical equation.
items.answer: (i) Ethanol reacts with sodium metal to liberate hydrogen, whereas methyl ethanoate does not. The two differ in their functional group – ethanol has the alcoholic –OH group while methyl ethanoate has the ester –COO– group – and since the functional group decides the chemical behaviour, their chemical properties differ. (ii) Methyl ethanoate is an ester and it has a pleasant fruity smell, which is why it is used in making perfumes. (iii) CH₃CH₂OH --conc. H₂SO₄, Δ--> CH₂=CH₂ + H₂O. Ethanol gets dehydrated with excess hot conc. H₂SO₄ to form ethene and H₂O; conc. H₂SO₄ acts as a dehydrating agent.
items.ocr: The printed equation in (iii) shows 'conc. HNO₃' over the arrow, which contradicts both the question and the very next line of its own solution ('Ethanol gets dehydrated with conc. H₂SO₄'). The solution text wins: the reagent is conc. H₂SO₄. Arrow restored.

items.stem: (a) Define the term functional group. Identify the group present in the two structures printed below: (i) a carbon atom joined to two hydrogen atoms by single bonds and to an oxygen atom by a double bond (H–CHO); (ii) a CH₃ group joined to a carbon that is double bonded to one oxygen and single bonded to an –OH group (CH₃–COOH). (b) What happens when 5% alkaline KMnO₄ solution is added drop by drop to warm ethanol taken in a test tube? State the role of alkaline KMnO₄ solution in this reaction.
items.answer: (a) A functional group is an atom or group of atoms – the reactive part of a compound – which largely determines the chemical properties of that compound. (i) The structure is methanal, HCHO; the group present is the aldehyde group, –CHO. (ii) The structure is ethanoic acid, CH₃COOH; the group present is the carboxylic acid group, –COOH. (b) The pink colour of the alkaline KMnO₄ disappears as it is added drop by drop, because it oxidises the warm ethanol to ethanoic acid: CH₃CH₂OH + 2[O] --KMnO₄/KOH--> CH₃COOH + H₂O. Alkaline KMnO₄ acts as an oxidising agent.
items.ocr: Structures (i) and (ii) print as broken LaTeX line drawings with stray bond bars; described in words in the stem using the names the worked solution gives them ('(i) Methanal, (ii) Ethanoic acid'). The printed answer names only the compounds; the functional groups (–CHO, –COOH) that the question actually asks for are added. Arrow restored.

items.stem: An organic compound with molecular formula C₃H₈O reacts with sodium metal to produce hydrogen gas. Deduce the possible structure of the compound. Write the balanced chemical equation of the reaction.
items.answer: Since the compound liberates hydrogen gas with sodium metal, it must contain the alcoholic –OH functional group. The possible structure of the compound is propanol: CH₃–CH₂–CH₂–OH (each of the three carbon atoms completes four bonds, the end carbon carrying the –O–H group). 2CH₃CH₂CH₂OH + 2Na → 2CH₃CH₂CH₂O⁻Na⁺ + H₂(g), i.e. propanol gives sodium propoxide and hydrogen gas.
items.ocr: The printed molecular formula lost its subscripts ('C H O'); restored to C₃H₈O from the worked solution, which identifies the compound as propanol. The printed solution labels the product 'sodium ethoxide'; from its own formula CH₃CH₂CH₂O⁻Na⁺ the product is sodium propoxide, so the solution's formula wins. Printed 'Proanol' repaired to 'propanol'.

items.stem: Name the compound formed when ethanol is heated in excess of conc. sulphuric acid at 443 K. Also write the chemical equation of the reaction stating the role of conc. sulphuric acid in it. What would happen if hydrogen is added to the product of this reaction in the presence of catalysts such as palladium or nickel?
items.answer: When ethanol is heated in excess of conc. H₂SO₄ at 443 K, ethene is formed: CH₃CH₂OH --conc. H₂SO₄, 443 K--> CH₂=CH₂ + H₂O. Concentrated sulphuric acid acts as a dehydrating agent, removing a molecule of water from ethanol. If hydrogen is then added to ethene in the presence of a catalyst such as palladium or nickel, an addition (hydrogenation) reaction takes place and ethane is formed: CH₂=CH₂ + H₂ --Ni or Pd (catalyst)--> CH₃–CH₃.
items.ocr: The printed solution says 'Ethene reacts with hydrogen ... to form ethene', but its own equation gives CH₃–CH₃; the solution's equation wins, so the product is ethane. Arrows restored.

items.stem: Write three different chemical reactions showing the conversion of ethanoic acid to sodium ethanoate. Write balanced chemical equation in each case. Write the name of the reactants and the products other than ethanoic acid and sodium ethanoate in each case.
items.answer: (1) With sodium hydroxide: CH₃COOH + NaOH → CH₃COONa + H₂O. Other reactant – sodium hydroxide (a base); other product – water. (2) With sodium metal: 2CH₃COOH + 2Na → 2CH₃COONa + H₂. Other reactant – sodium; other product – hydrogen gas. (3) With sodium carbonate: 2CH₃COOH + Na₂CO₃ → 2CH₃COONa + H₂O + CO₂. Other reactant – sodium carbonate; other products – water and carbon dioxide.
items.ocr: No year tag is printed with this answer. The printed answer block shows only two equations although the question asks for three, and its sodium equation is mis-set as '2CH₃COOH + 2Na → CH₃COONa + H₂O' (the sodium reaction gives H₂, not H₂O); balanced and corrected here. The third reaction, with sodium carbonate, is not legible in the scan and has been supplied so the answer covers the three conversions asked for.

items.stem: An organic acid X is a liquid which often freezes during winter time in cold countries. It has molecular formula C₂H₄O₂. On warming with ethanol in the presence of a few drops of conc. H₂SO₄ a compound Y with sweet smell is formed. (i) Identify X and Y. (ii) Write chemical equation for the reaction involved.
items.answer: (i) Compound X is CH₃COOH, ethanoic acid (glacial acetic acid) – it freezes in cold countries because its melting point is 290 K. Compound Y is CH₃COOCH₂CH₃ (CH₃COOC₂H₅), ethyl ethanoate, an ester with a sweet smell. (ii) CH₃COOH + C₂H₅OH --conc. H₂SO₄--> CH₃COOC₂H₅ + H₂O.
items.ocr: The equation prints with the products stacked underneath the arrow in LaTeX rather than after it; rewritten with → . Printed 'Write chemical equation or the reaction' repaired to 'for the reaction'.

items.stem: Write chemical equations along with necessary conditions for the following changes to take place: (i) Ethanol to ethanoic acid. (ii) Ethanoic acid to sodium acetate. (iii) Methane to chloromethane.
items.answer: (i) CH₃CH₂OH --alkaline KMnO₄ + heat--> CH₃COOH (oxidation of ethanol to ethanoic acid). (ii) CH₃COOH + NaOH → CH₃COONa + H₂O (ethanoic acid with a base gives sodium acetate and water). (iii) CH₄ + Cl₂ --sunlight--> CH₃Cl + HCl (a substitution reaction in the presence of sunlight).
items.ocr: No year tag is printed with this answer. In (iii) the product printed as 'CH Cl' with the subscript lost; restored to CH₃Cl. Arrows restored.

items.stem: (a) What is denatured alcohol? (b) How many covalent bonds does a molecule of ethane (C₂H₆) have? Draw its structure to justify your answer.
items.answer: (a) When ethanol is mixed with methanol or with some poisonous substances such as copper sulphate, pyridine etc., it becomes unfit for drinking. Such an alcohol is called denatured alcohol. (b) A molecule of ethane has seven single covalent bonds – one C–C bond and six C–H bonds. Structure: H₃C–CH₃, i.e. H–C(H)(H)–C(H)(H)–H, in which each carbon atom is joined to three hydrogen atoms and to the other carbon atom.
items.ocr: Printed answer label 'd When ethanol is mixed...' is a damaged '(a)'. The ethane structure is a worked-solution drawing, so no image is attached and the structure is given in linear form.

items.stem: (a) Complete the following reactions and name the main product formed in each case: (i) CH₃CH₂OH --alkaline KMnO₄--> (ii) CH₃COOC₂H₅ + NaOH --> (iii) CH₄ + Cl₂ --sunlight-->
items.answer: (i) CH₃CH₂OH --alkaline KMnO₄ + heat--> CH₃COOH. Main product: ethanoic acid (acetic acid); ethanol is oxidised. (ii) CH₃COOC₂H₅ + NaOH → CH₃COONa + C₂H₅OH. Main products: sodium ethanoate and ethanol; this alkaline hydrolysis of an ester is called saponification. (iii) CH₄ + Cl₂ --sunlight--> CH₃Cl + HCl. Main product: chloromethane (methyl chloride), along with hydrogen chloride; this is a substitution reaction.
items.ocr: No year tag is printed. The question text lost all subscripts and arrows ('CH CH OH Alkaline KMnO4', 'CH COOC H5 NaOH', 'CH4 + Cl2 Sunlight'); restored. The answer block, which sits on the next page, is almost entirely destroyed LaTeX with only 'CH₃CH₂OH', 'CH₃COOC₂H₅ ... NaOH ... CH₃COONa ... Ethanol' and 'CH₄ + Cl₂' legible; the three equations were reconstructed from those fragments and from the identical reactions printed with question 241.

items.stem: An organic compound X is an essential constituent of wine and beer. X is responsible for the intoxication caused by these drinks. Oxidation of X yields an organic acid Y which is present in vinegar. Name the compounds X and Y and write their structural formulae.
items.answer: The compound X is ethanol, C₂H₅OH, while Y is ethanoic acid (acetic acid), CH₃COOH. Structural formulae: ethanol – H₃C–CH₂–O–H, each carbon completing four bonds with hydrogen atoms; ethanoic acid – H₃C–C(=O)–O–H, in which the carboxyl carbon is doubly bonded to one oxygen and singly bonded to the –OH group. The conversion is an oxidation: CH₃CH₂OH --alkaline KMnO₄ (or acidified K₂Cr₂O₇)--> CH₃COOH.

items.stem: (a) Draw the structure of ethyne (C₂H₂). (b) List any two differences between soaps and detergents.
items.answer: (a) Ethyne: H–C≡C–H. The two carbon atoms are joined by a triple bond (three shared electron pairs) and each carbon atom is joined to one hydrogen atom by a single bond. (b) (i) Soaps are sodium salts of long chain fatty acids, whereas detergents are sodium or potassium salts of sulphonic acids of long chain hydrocarbons. (ii) Soaps cannot be used with hard water (they form scum), but detergents work well with both hard and soft water.
